A LITTLE MORE CONTEXT

Sources & model notes

This is a conceptual illustration of semantic-ID generative retrieval, inspired by TIGER. The items, codes, relationships, and vector positions are illustrative.

Recommender Systems with Generative RetrievalRajput et al. · TIGER · 2023 ↗Efficient vector similarity searchGoogle Research · ScaNN · 2020 ↗Amazon.com Recommendations: Item-to-Item Collaborative FilteringLinden, Smith & York · 2003 ↗
  • Semantic codes come from learned quantization, not a fixed human taxonomy. Similar prefixes are possible, not guaranteed.
  • Three codes distinguish our tiny demo catalog. Real systems must handle collisions, for example with an extra disambiguation token.
  • Generation is conditioned on history and previous output codes. Practical systems search multiple sequences and handle invalid IDs with constraints, filtering, or catalog validation.
  • The beam-search demo uses a width of three and permits only valid catalog prefixes. Scores are illustrative products of conditional token probabilities; implementations commonly add log probabilities. Paths compete globally at each step. Pruned paths cannot return, so beam search does not guarantee the globally best sequences.
  • Catalog constraints are a teaching choice here; the original TIGER experiments discuss filtering invalid IDs. See GENRE for a primary example of constrained identifier generation.
  • ANN systems can also use Transformers and user histories. The comparison is about candidate retrieval, before optional filtering and ranking.
  • There is no universal winner on speed or quality. Training, catalog updates, and serving constraints matter.
